item.title: ‘World-class’: Erik Spoelstra gives ‘the greatest compliment you could give’ to one Knicks star
item.description: Photo by Eric Espada/Getty Images Erik Spoelstra is widely regarded as one of the best coaches in the NBA. The 56-year-old has turned the Miami Heat’s season around by winning 11 of his side’s last 14 games after losing each of his first four. On Friday, Spoelstra secured another win, this time against the New York Knicks, but before the game, he lavished praise on the defending champions’ best player – Jalen Brunson. Erik Spoelstra says Jalen Brunson has ‘the heart of a champion’ Brunson is arguably the biggest reason why the New York Knicks won the NBA championship last season. The 30-year-old won the NBA Cup MVP, Eastern Conference Finals MVP and NBA Finals MVP awards as he led the Knicks to their first title in 53 years. Spoelstra has faced Brunson plenty of times over the years and even coached him for Team USA at the 2023 FIBA Men’s Basketball World Cup. Ahead of the game on Friday, the Heat coach raved about Brunson and what he has always felt about the Knicks superstar. He said, as per Jared Schwartz of the New York Post on X : “He has the heart of a champion and I think he’s had that for a long time. “The one thing, we faced him in the playoffs a few years ago, and you feel him as a competitor. And that’s probably the greatest compliment you could give him, is he’s a world-class, top-percentile competitor. “He transcends what his size may be, and he’s going to make you take note of him every single possession that he’s out on the court. And in the moments of truth, that’s probably when he showed up the biggest. I have respect for him as a competitor as much as I have for anyone in this league.” The Miami Heat ended up beating the New York Knicks on Friday, with Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo producing a combined 47 points and 30 rebounds. However, Brunson caused them plenty of problems, scoring 27 points and recording three rebounds, eight assists and three steals. He came close to tying the game in the end, but Davion Mitchell saved the day for the Heat. The Knicks are now 12-7 for the season, which is not awful, but they need to get a lot better to have a chance of repeating what they did in the last campaign. item.title: WWE faces backlash for Bronson Reed tribute using ‘AI-generated’ voice
item.description: The professional wrestling community was struck by tragedy on Friday night, with news that Jerinrmaine Haley, known under his ring name Bronson Reed, passed away suddenly at age 38 . According to a statement from WWE , he died due to “medical complications.” WWE announced the news shortly before SmackDown on Friday night, which forced the company to scramble to put together a pre-show tribute. The company also shared a tribute on social media , featuring the on-screen graphic shown on SmackDown , along with a voiceover that sounded like commentator Michael Cole. When the tribute dropped on social media, however, something was amiss, and fans immediately took to social media, accusing WWE of using an AI-generated voiceover. Several comments were calling out the company for its “disrespect” and lack of effort put into giving Reed the proper tribute. MORE: Watch Kevin Owens honor Bronson Reed with in-ring tribute, speech at WWE Athens WWE Called Out Over Bronson Reed Tribute Jan 26, 2024; St. Petersburg, FL, USA; Bronson Reed during the WWE Media Junket at Hilton Carillion Park. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect (Reuters) “ WWE remembers the legacy of Jermaine Haley , also known as Bronson Reed,” WWE wrote on social media. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as his friends, co-workers, and fans.” The voiceover was a step too far for the WWE faithful and loyal Reed fans. “Giving your life to a company and entertaining the fans only for them to put a voice prompt into ChatGPT when you die. Incredibly dystopian,” one fan wrote. “ Just don’t do a voiceover if it’s that inconvenient .” Another added, “If not one of the 10 most abjectly evil things to be done in and/or by this company, an AI-voiced tribute video stands out as one of the most immediately upsetting and gross things this company’s ever done.” MORE: WWE Survivor Series 2026: Predictions and match card analysis Other fans were extremely disappointed in the lack of effort that went into Friday night’s tribute. However, there should be a more thoughtful and proper tribute on Saturday night at WWE Survivor Series: WarGames at Daikin Park in Houston, Texas. If the voice truly is AI-generated, it’s a major misstep from WWE, even if most of the top talent was booked at live house shows or traveling to Houston for Survivor Series . item.description: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 20: Head coach Buzz Williams of the Maryland Terrapins retrieves a shoe from the court during the second half against the Wagner Seahawks at Xfinity Center on November 20, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maryland has had an interesting time with coaches since Gary Williams retired. Mark Turgeon wasn’t horrible, but he wasn’t a great fit, either. He got there in 2011, and left in December of 2021, under intense pressure from the fan base. After a brief interim stint by Danny Manning, Turgeon’s successor was Kevin Willard, who stayed for three years. He left over money, basically, unable to get the funding he felt the basketball program deserved. Maryland hired Buzz Williams to replace him, and so far, it’s been another step down. The level of fan revolt is much like what we saw at Wake Forest when Jeff Bzdelik was hired and, subsequently, shunned. And by shunned we mean like an Amish shun. He was eventually driven out of his job. Then he was replaced by Buzz Williams. His hiring was treated much like that of Bzdelik: online at least, Maryland fans were incredulous. In his first season last year, Maryland finished 12-21, and so far this year, the Terps are 3-4, with wins over Bucknell, Alcorn State, and Wagner. The losses were to Georgetown, Virginia, Tennessee, San Diego State, and Oregon. According to the Field of 68, Williams is now 2-23 against top 80 KenPom teams. The fans are ready to dump him now, but we understand his buyout as of December is still about $25 million, so that may not happen. Keep in mind that the Terps already have to pay former football coach Mike Locksley’s buyout, which is close to $10 million, and about another $3 million, and have lost about $36 million over the last six years. Under those circumstances, firing Williams is going to be very difficult to do. Given his history and his publicly stated conviction that he prefers to change jobs before he wears out his welcome, we could imagine Williams either taking another job this spring or reaching an agreement with Maryland. In the meantime, barring a major turnaround, the fan reactions are not settling down anytime soon. The funniest part, though, comes from Tom Izzo, via sophomore Cam Ward. item.title: Joe Burrow praises Colbie Young’s work ethic after first NFL touchdown
item.description: It was an ugly night all-around for the Cincinnati Bengals in Washington, though it did have some bright spots. The weather was part of the ugliness, but the manner in which the Cincinnati Bengals played on Monday Night Football was the remainder of said unsightliness. After slogging to a 10-0 lead, the Bengals appeared to be uninspired for the final two quarters of the game (maybe even more), letting a should-be win slip through their fingers—metaphorically and realistically speaking. Even so, there were a couple of bright spots on an otherwise disappointing evening. After the Commanders tied the game with just under 12 minutes remaining in the third quarter, Cincinnati’s offense was on the move for what would essentially be the last time in the game. Needing a score to try and pull away from Washington’s scrappy efforts, Joe Burrow found rookie Colbie Young for his first touchdown catch as an NFL receiver. Joe Burrow extending the play and finding Colbie Young in the end zone for his first career touchdown reception in the NFL. pic.twitter.com/LVab2j2UZO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 It was a vintage Burrow play, as he rolled right when the play broke down and found Young in the corner of the end zone. It was a critical play at the time, as the team was largely struggling on offense, and the Bengals regained the lead at 17-10. That was Young’s only catch on two targets against Washington, and only his second on the 2026 season, but it was a gigantic one from an overall game perspective. The Bengals went on to lose, but Young proved to be a bright spot in an otherwise ugly night. And it could be the start of a bigger role moving forward. During his weekly press conference, Burrow made sure to point out Young’s work ethic as part of why he’s growing into his role within the offense. “Seems to never make the same mistake twice. Works hard to be better,” Burrow said of Young. The rookie wide receiver has seen increased snaps with Andrei Iosivas still sitting on injured reserve. And, like Iosivas, Young is in that third receiver role that attempts to clear out space for Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, while also being a blocker in the run game, and occasionally being called upon in the explosive offense. While he’s still growing in the role, this first touchdown reception gives optimism about his development. When the Bengals drafted him in the third round this year, they knew that he was a height/weight/speed/athleticism specimen who could stretch the field but needed polish. The fact that Young’s touchdown reception was a short-yardage one in the red zone on a broken play should catch the attention of the staff. We will see how that ends up translating down the stretch.

item.title: Borussia Mönchengladbach supporters carry on with ‘bingo card’ protest against kickoff times
item.description: Borussia Mönchengladbach supporters carry on with ‘bingo card’ protest against kickoff times Borussia Mönchengladbach supporters are carrying on with their “bingo” protest against 2026/27 Bundesliga fixture scheduling, culminating in a brief interruption during Friday evening’s 3-3 draw against Werder Bremen. The latest demonstration follows weeks of complaints about inconvenient kick-off times, with Gladbach supporters previously introducing a satirical campaign dubbed “Ansetzungs-Bullshit-Bingo” (fixture-scheduling bullshit bingo). The protests centre on the German Football League’s (DFL) decision to schedule three of Gladbach’s longest away journeys on Friday evenings within the space of just over a month. Matches against VfB Stuttgart, Hamburger SV, and Werder Bremen were all assigned 20:30 kick-offs, creating considerable logistical difficulties for travelling supporters. Gladbach supporters protest against three Friday-night away fixtures Friday’s encounter at the Weserstadion was temporarily interrupted in the 49th minute after golf balls were thrown onto the playing surface from the Gladbach away section. Referee Felix Zwayer briefly halted proceedings while the objects were cleared. The demonstration followed Franck Honorat’s goal shortly after halftime, which had given Gladbach a 2-1 lead. The visitors subsequently extended their advantage to 3-1 before conceding twice in the closing stages, with Niclas Füllkrug rescuing a point for Bremen in stoppage time. The underlying grievance had been apparent since September, when the DFL announced the precise kick-off times for matchdays five through eleven. Supporters wishing to attend all three fixtures in Stuttgart, Hamburg, and Bremen faced approximately 2,350 kilometres of return travel. Each journey involved hundreds of kilometres on a working day, with many fans potentially forced to take time off, leave work early, or arrange overnight accommodation. The first of those fixtures took place at Stuttgart’s MHPArena on October 23. Get German Football News was present for Gladbach’s dramatic 3-2 victory over Stuttgart. The Gladbach fans first raised their bingo card at this fixture. German football magazine 11FREUNDE subsequently highlighted their protest in its regular Kurvenschau examination of German fan culture, emphasizing the inconvenience of requiring supporters to travel more than 400 kilometres to Stuttgart on a Friday. The bingo concept turned the seemingly endless frustrations surrounding Bundesliga scheduling into a satirical protest, with supporters using the language of a familiar game to draw attention to kick-off arrangements they considered increasingly unreasonable. The campaign reflected a grievance that long predates the current season. Gladbach’s organized supporters have repeatedly advocated for more matches to be scheduled at the traditional Saturday 15:30 kick-off time. item.title: Red Sox Floated as Potential Landing Spot for Former No. 1 Overall Pick
item.description: Red Sox Floated as Potential Landing Spot for Former No. 1 Overall Pick originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Reports indicate the Red Sox are still looking to improve on the mound this offseason, and among the options that make sense, going after a former No. 1 overall pick could be at the top of that list. Casey Mize, the Padres free agent, has been very impressive over the past few years. There have been moments when Mize has been a bit disappointing because of the injuries that he's dealt with, and in 2026, in the second half for San Diego, he posted a 7.46 ERA, but what I'm looking at is that 2.70 ERA he posted in 16 starts for the Tigers in the first half. Ian Browne of MLB.com believes he could be an option for the Red Sox, adding that he fits exactly what Craig Breslow could be looking for. "After a strong 16-start sample last season for the Tigers (2.70 ERA), Mize faded after the Trade Deadline deal that sent him to the Padres, as evidenced by a 7.46 ERA in 10 starts. The ERA was inflated by two rough outings. "He gave up eight runs in 3 1/3 innings in his first start for the Padres at Arizona on Aug. 5 and gave up a seven-spot in four innings in his final start of the regular season on Sept. 25 -- again against the D-backs. However, health contributed to Mize's late-season slide. He slipped on the dugout steps in August and ended the season on the 15-day injured list with a right ankle sprain. Breslow likes extension with his pitchers, and Mize was in the 83rd percentile in that department in '26," Browne wrote . The impressive first half with Detroit shows what Mize can do when things are right. The struggles in San Diego, as Browne pointed out, might not have been as bad as they make it seem in his numbers because of a couple of bad starts. What I was a bit worried about with Mize is that he only struck out 25 hitters in 44.2 innings. Not to say that he's a big swing-and-miss guy, never striking out more than 139 hitters in a season, but he has the stuff to get outs. He feels like a guy who might have to take a one- or two-year deal to raise his value. If that ends up being the case, it would make a lot of sense for the Red Sox to have some level of interest in him. item.title: Celtics Insider Throws Shade at Jayson Tatum for Jaylen Brown Reason
item.description: Celtics Insider Throws Shade at Jayson Tatum for Jaylen Brown Reason originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Celtics look very different from how they did a year ago, a couple of seasons ago, and all in between. Typically, we're used to seeing the Celtics be one of the best teams in the NBA. While Boston hasn't been terrible this year, sitting at 12-7, it's not unfair to say it's been somewhat disappointing, at least over the past week and a half. When Boston decided to move on from Jaylen Brown in a deal to land Paul George, it was always going to lead to ridiculous takes about Jayson Tatum not being the best player on the roster since he entered the league. That's continued to be the case, and Sherrod Blakely was the latest one to bring it up, adding that he doesn't believe that Tatum can play with this roster because it's not good enough, but Brown was able to a year ago. "This [team] is the Transformer that was made out of bits and pieces of sh*t that people didn't want...Jaylen can work with that...[Tatum] needs better players around him to be a great player,” Sherrod Blakely said . Without a doubt, the Celtics had a nice regular season last year, going 56-26 and finishing in second place in the Eastern Conference. Brown was very good last season as well, but there should also be some context added. There were multiple players on the Celtics who stepped up in a big way last year, including Payton Pritchard, who averaged 17 points and shot 37.7% from 3-point range. Whether people want to say that was because of what Brown can do for his teammates, that's one thing, but Pritchard hasn't been the same player this year, averaging just 12.8 points per game and shooting 33.6% from the field. As I've said before, I see this more as an issue with the Celtics as a whole not playing good basketball instead of just blaming Tatum, who admittedly hasn't played as well as we're used to seeing him, but it's also not ridiculous considering that he’s still working back from a very difficult injury to come back from. item.title: Pittsburgh Steelers fans chanted something wild that Aaron Rodgers would hate against Broncos
item.description: Photo by Rob Tringali/Sportschrome/Getty Images Friday night provided the Pittsburgh Steelers fans with an opportunity to see what their future without Aaron Rodgers looks like. It has been a strange week in Pittsburgh, with the 42-year-old quarterback attempting to leave a trail of destruction behind him on his way out of the building. Instead, it appears to have galvanised the team, with the Steelers securing a big win over the Denver Broncos. Despite the football game going on, Rodgers remained the biggest talking point, with some Steelers fans voicing their thoughts about their former quarterback with a chant that is unlikely to go down well within the Rodgers household. Pittsburgh Steelers fans vent anger with Aaron Rodgers chant vs Broncos Although the season had by no means been a disaster, it was apparent that something was not right between Rodgers and Mike McCarthy. However, no one would have expected how this week would have panned out, with fans allowing their frustrations with Rodgers to be known. “F*** you, Rodgers,” fans were heard singing on Amazon Prime’s broadcast of the game inside the fourth quarter. Footage of the chant was shared on X . It is only natural that what went down this week would divide opinions. Some will feel as if Rodgers’ outburst was to highlight McCarthy’s issues, which is something the Steelers fans may deserve to be aware of. However, there is also a clear feeling that Rodgers wanted to drag the Steelers organisation down with him. Even if he was to air out the dirty laundry, perhaps he could have waited until the offseason to do his interview with Pat McAfee. In true Rodgers style, that was not the case, with the 42-year-old looking set to end his NFL career covered in as much controversy as possible. Rodgers has been labelled a bully by some fans, and these Steelers fans in attendance on Friday certainly voiced their thoughts. item.title: ‘Cannot interact like…’ – Skip Bayless lashes out at Luka Doncic’s courtside altercation with fans
item.description: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images Skip Bayless has delivered a strong verdict on Luka Doncic’s interaction with the San Antonio Spurs fans after the game. Luka Doncic’s night ended in disappointment after the Los Angeles Lakers succumbed to a 99-96 loss against their closest Western Conference rivals on Friday night. His abysmal three-point shooting was a big factor in the loss, and the negativity was compounded by what happened after the game. While making his way off the court, Luka ended up in an altercation with two fans. The Slovenian star threw his wristband into the crowd, and then got shoved by a fan after he went back to retrieve it after they said something. The incident caused a lot of commotion on social media, and now Skip Bayless has spoken candidly about it. Skip Bayless says Luka Doncic should not behave in this manner with NBA fans Doncic’s stellar start to the season has seen Bayless, one of his biggest detractors, claim that he has been ‘won over’ by the Lakers superstar. However, the last few games have seen Luka slump, and with this latest fan interaction, Bayless seems far from happy with the Slovenian. After the video of Doncic’s exchange with the fan went viral, the talking head was quick to post on X about how he thinks that Luka should have known better than to do that. “Looked like a man and woman objected to how hard Luka threw her his (I think) wristband. When they said something Luka stormed back, snatched it back, man pushed him. Luka cannot interact like that with fans,” Skip said about the situation. Doncic gave a succinct explanation when asked about his side of the story. The star is naturally more focused on the loss and his own 14-of-31 performance than on this particular moment. It remains to be seen if the NBA will take any further action, as any physical altercation with fans is taken extremely seriously. item.title: Real Madrid’s 17-year-old defensive gem shines at U17 World Cup after switching Spain for France
item.description: Real Madrid’s 17-year-old defensive gem shines at U17 World Cup after switching Spain for France Real Madrid’s next generation is beginning to take shape, with the academy producing a number of gems who have genuine first-team prospects. Los Blancos have placed a lot of emphasis on developing talent in the academy, even if not all players go on to make it to the first team. While players like Thiago Pitarch earn first-team opportunities at the Santiago Bernabeu , others, like Nico Paz and Jacobo Ramon, are sold for significant sums. Now, according to MARCA , another Los Blancos academy prospect, Leo Lemaitre, has been one of the standout defenders at the U-17 World Cup in Qatar. The teenager switched allegiance to represent France rather than Spain and has impressed at the tournament. Leo Lemaitre impressing with France Lemaitre joined Real Madrid at 12 and has steadily climbed through the ranks at La Fabrica over the years. View this post on Instagram A post shared by @leolemaxx He signed a contract extension until 2028 in January and trained with Castilla during pre-season. He has since become part of the Juvenil A set-up. Having made six appearances for Spain’s U-15s and two for the U-16s, the teenager has now switched allegiance to France. His French father, Nicolas, explained that the family maintained close ties to the country, prompting Leo to make the switch. France Under-17 coach Jose Alcocer admitted that the youngster had been difficult to identify because he played outside France and had previously used his mother’s surname. However, the decision already seems to be paying off, with Leo forming an excellent partnership with Mohamed Sylla. Real Madrid have another promising defensive talent The 17-year-old’s numbers in the tournament have been impressive. He is averaging 7.87 ball recoveries per match. Leo has also completed 92% of his passes and 77% of his long balls, showcasing his composure with the ball at his feet. Having a central defender who is comfortable on the ball is important in modern-day football. Jose Mourinho’s immense trust in Dean Huijsen is an example of how much he values composure on the ball. Lemaitre has shown in the tournament that he is good not only at winning the ball back but also at playing it forward. While talk of a potential first-team spot may be premature, his talent is obvious. If his development matches his potential, Real Madrid may have a special player on their hands, and it remains to be seen how Lemaitre fares in the coming seasons.

item.title: Fans want Wizards rookie banned from NBA for punching Rob Dillingham in heated NBA G League game

Many thought that would happen during the recent NBA G League game between the Westchester Knicks and the Capital City Go-Go. item.title: Five of the Premier League's greatest loan cult heroes
item.description: Five of the Premier League's greatest loan cult heroes Football fans are told never to fall in love with a loan player. But when a temporary transfer produces performances of such quality, it's almost impossible for them not to win hearts. Ronald Araujo is the latest loanee to become a fan favourite, with the defender earning Anfield admiration at Liverpool. Should the Reds opt against a permanent deal, Araujo could join the long list of Premier League loan cult heroes. Carlos Tevez - West Ham Carlos Tevez 's move to West Ham remains one of the most infamous deals in Premier League history. West Ham's shock swoop for the Argentine forward and compatriot Javier Mascherano stunned football, as two of world football's best up-and-coming talents headed to the East End. While Mascherano muddled through a forgettable six months before leaving, Tevez dug deep to make an impact. After a slow start, the forward's form caught fire. He scored his first goal in March, and ended the season with seven goals in nine games. West Ham had been 10 points from safety in early March, but a remarkable run carried the club to safety. Tevez's winner at Manchester United on the final day confirmed Premier League status, and cemented him as a West Ham hero. However, the deal proved controversial. West Ham were found to have breached third-party ownership regulations, with the rights to both Tevez and Mascherano partially held by agent Kia Joorabchian's company, Media Sports Investment (MSI). A messy fallout followed, with Sheffield United, who were relegated at West Ham's expense, eventually receiving £20m in an out-of-court settlement in 2009. Henrik Larsson - Manchester United Manchester United signed Henrik Larsson on a short-term loan deal in 2007, as the Swedish striker arrived to add depth to Sir Alex Ferguson's squad. Larsson had turned down approaches from the Premier League during a decorated career at Celtic, where he scored 242 goals in 313 appearances. In the latter stages of his career, a call from United saw him head to England. He scored three times in 13 appearances, but his impact extended far beyond goals. "In his last game at Middlesbrough, we were winning 2-1 and Henrik went back to play in midfield and ran his balls off," Ferguson wrote in his autobiography. item.title: Why The NBA’s New Draft Lottery Could Cripple The Trade Deadline
item.description: NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum announces that the Chicago Bulls had won the seventh pick during the NBA basketball draft lottery Tuesday, May 14, 2019, in Chicago. (AP Photo/Nuccio DiNuzzo) Copyright 2019 The Associated Press. All rights reserved The NBA’s February trade deadline has become an annual holiday for basketball fans. It’s the last chance for teams to make blockbuster additions that can upend the championship picture. However, the trade deadline may be a casualty of the NBA’s new draft lottery. In an effort to deter teams from tanking, the league completely overhauled its lottery system this past May. Previously, the teams with the three worst records all had a 14.0% chance of landing the No. 1 overall pick, and no team could fall more than four spots from where they finished in the standings. That’s no longer the case. Under the new lottery, the teams with three worst records have worse odds than the other seven teams that miss the play-in tournament. Those teams can now fall as low as the 12th overall pick, while the other 13 teams in the lottery—which includes the losers of the No. 7 vs. No. 8 play-in game—can drop as far as 16th. That’s not all. Teams are now prohibited from landing the No. 1 overall pick in back-to-back drafts via the lottery. They also can’t receive top-five picks in three straight years. While the new lottery might not completely dissuade teams from tanking, it should at least prevent the egregious shenanigans that have been on full display late in the past few seasons. However, the decreased odds for the teams in the so-called “relegation zone” could also deter teams from embarking upon trade-deadline teardowns, even if that would otherwise be in their best long-term interests. “There will be less sellers than ever before,” one Eastern Conference team strategist told Jake Fischer of The Stein Line in mid-November. That doesn’t mean this year’s trade deadline will be a complete bust. In fact, a few teams are uniquely equipped to ignore the new lottery system and tear down with impunity. But teams that do control their own 2027 first-round pick will have to think twice before taking a stick of dynamite to their roster at this year’s trade deadline. Which Would-Be Sellers Might Stand Pat? If the previous lottery system were still in place, the Sacramento Kings might be the NBA’s most obvious seller at this year’s trade deadline. At 2-16, the Kings are already 7.5 games behind the 10th-seeded Oklahoma City Thunder for the final spot in the West’s play-in tournament. They also have the NBA’s worst net rating , which suggests their record isn’t simply a byproduct of bad early-season luck. The Kings have been open for business on Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis for the better part of a year (if not longer), although they’ve yet to find a taker for either one. item.description: Brian Barry-Murphy will lean on the likes of Ollie Tanner, who scored in Cardiff's 2-0 win over Swansea in 2023, in his first south Wales derby [Huw Evans Picture Agency] It can be difficult to change the narrative in sport. Take Cardiff City and their rivalry with Swansea City. For years, a certain idea had taken hold, that the Swans - their players, staff, the club as a whole - had a better understanding of what the south Wales derby meant, and that innate grasp of its significance had given them the upper hand. Results have supported the theory. Since a nine-year period at the start of this century where there were no derbies, Swansea have won 11 out of 21 and become the first team in the fixture's century-long history to do the double – that is, to win both league meetings in one season – before repeating the feat the following campaign. Once a pattern is set in motion, it can take some stopping but, by winning their past two home derbies, Cardiff felt the tide might have been turning. Granted, the most recent of those triumphs still ended with their relegation to League One two seasons ago, but there was at least a feeling that the hoodoo had been lifted. Nearly two years have passed since the last south Wales derby. In that time, Cardiff have made an instant return to the Championship under head coach Brian Barry-Murphy, who has introduced a refreshingly bold and attacking style of play, built around a core of young local players. They are still behind their neighbours, though. Cardiff travel to Swansea on Sunday 17th in the table, nine places and nine points adrift of their opponents. The Bluebirds have caught the eye with their performances this season but, for all their ambition and stylish dominance of possession, the defensive risks that come attached mean that they are still searching for a first away win of the campaign. Ashley Williams celebrating with Garry Monk amid delirium across three sides of what was then the Liberty Stadium following a Wayne Routledge goal. It was February 2014, and Swansea City and Cardiff City were both under pressure thanks to the threat of Premier League relegation. Swansea had sacked manager Michael Laudrup only four days before the game, and placed club skipper Monk in charge for the biggest fixture of that or any season in which south Wales' two premier clubs were in the same division. It proved a wise move, as Swansea triumphed in the derby and - unlike Cardiff - won their battle to stay in the top flight. Routledge's strike put Swansea on the way to a comprehensive 3-0 win – and sent Williams hurtling towards the technical area to embrace his long-time centre-back partner. It was more rugby tackle than hug when he got there, with Williams almost knocking Monk off his feet after Swansea had taken the first step towards victory over their rivals. "They're the good moments in football," Williams says now, as the interim Swansea boss prepares for Sunday's latest derby edition. "Some go for you and some go against you, and when they go for you, you want to enjoy it. "I think he (Monk) probably thought I was coming to ask him something tactical, or maybe he'd just been annoying me all week and I just wanted to rugby tackle him... you can just see the relief and the enjoyment, the passion in that moment." Twelve years later, Williams is the man holding the fort following a managerial change. The circumstances this time are different. Monk swapped the dressing room for the manager's office after a run of six defeats in eight games had left Swansea only two points above the Premier League relegation zone. Williams, meanwhile, was parachuted back into his old club last week after Vitor Matos walked out on a Swans squad who had made a promising start to the season. The dugout is almost uncharted territory for Williams, even if he has been part of Wales' backroom team since September. The 42-year-old has spent most of his time doing punditry work since ending his playing career in 2021. This weekend it will be match of the season - in south Wales at least - rather than Match of the Day as Swansea do battle with their fiercest rivals. Would it not be simpler to watch on this Sunday with microphone in hand than to be barking orders on the touchline? item.title: 'They barely spoke to me' - Vitor Roque blasts Barcelona lack of support and reveals hidden injury battle during Camp Nou nightmare
item.description: FC Barcelona v Getafe CF - LaLiga EA Sports - Getty Images Sport Brazilian forward Vitor Roque has broken his silence on a turbulent period with Barcelona, detailing a lack of communication from coaching staff that hampered his integration. The 21-year-old arrived at Camp Nou with high expectations but struggled to cement a place in the side before eventually returning to his homeland. Injury setbacks and isolation derailed Roque's Catalan dream Roque joined Barcelona from Athletico Paranaense in January 2024 as an 18-year-old, but his Catalan spell quickly stalled. He scored twice in 16 appearances before heading to Real Betis on loan and returning permanently to Brazil with Palmeiras in February 2025. In an interview with AS , the striker revealed that an unoperated syndesmotic injury suffered before leaving Brazil hampered him from day one. Arriving in Spain in severe pain, he spent much of his early stint in physiotherapy rather than competing at full fitness. Roque opens up on playing through pain and coaching silence Roque explained that fulfilling his dream move turned difficult because he entered Camp Nou carrying an untreated injury. "I went to Barcelona when I was 18. It was a dream come true: playing for one of the biggest clubs in the world," he said. "It was a bit difficult. I went there with a syndesmotic injury, which I should have had surgery for at Athletico Paranaense but didn’t. I arrived in a lot of pain - quite a lot, actually. "During that time, I was doing physiotherapy, trying to get into the best possible shape, but in the end we didn’t manage it. I wasn’t able to perform at the highest level in football and I think that was part of the process. I know that God has everything planned out, yes. It just didn’t work out there. Afterwards, I went to Betis and I couldn’t perform there either. But today at Palmeiras I feel good; I feel at home. People have helped me a lot and, thank God, I’m happy." Europe's impatience with young South American talents He also criticised the lack of patience and coaching communication shown to young arrivals adapting to a new language. "People think that when we young players arrive, we have to start playing at 100 per cent straight away, giving it our all and playing our best football, but that’s not how it works. It takes patience," he continued. "Sometimes we don’t have the time we need to settle in. We’re very young, and speaking a new language is really difficult. "Sometimes it’s important to have the manager’s support, and when I went to Barcelona, I didn’t have that. They barely spoke to me, you know? So I think you have to bear that in mind, and a lot of people don’t see it that way - they think you have to be ready from the very first minute." item.description: Mourinho’s bold experiment with veteran midfielder pays off as Real Madrid find their midfield solution Real Madrid had identified midfield as an area to reinforce back in the summer but faced a setback when Rodri rejected their offer to sign for Barcelona. However, despite missing out on the Ballon d’Or winner, Jose Mourinho did not feel the need to find an alternative in the transfer market. Instead, the Portuguese manager had already identified a solution in a player the club had signed. According to Diario AS , Mourinho was convinced that Bernardo Silva could play the role he had envisioned for Rodri. The Portuguese captain has since forged an excellent partnership with Aurelien Tchouameni, vindicating his manager’s trust. Mourinho’s gamble pays off Mourinho took a huge tactical gamble in trusting that Bernardo could help provide the balance Los Blancos need in midfield. Though not the most physically gifted, the former Man City captain possessed the intelligence, positional awareness and work rate to succeed in the position. Bernardo Silva has been indispensable for Madrid in recent weeks. (Picture credit: Real Madrid website) It did not start as expected, though. Bernardo struggled to establish himself following his arrival as he worked his way back to full fitness. However, the former Man City star has become an indispensable figure since Los Blancos ‘ 2-1 victory over Barcelona in October. Since the Clasico triumph, Bernardo has started every match, playing more than 86% of the available minutes and becoming one of Mourinho’s most trusted players. Bernardo proving his worth in midfield The 32-year-old has also put concerns about his physical abilities to bed. Against PSV, he covered 13.1 kilometres. That is much higher than Los Blancos ‘ average of around 10 kilometres per player per game, the lowest across Europe’s top five leagues. Mourinho got the gamble perfectly right with Bernardo. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Beyond all this, his greatest contribution has been the control he has brought to midfield through his ability to retain possession. Having played for so many years under Pep Guardiola, the midfielder is putting all that quality to use in Mourinho’s system. His partnership with Tchouameni also offers Real Madrid an interesting balance, with the Frenchman providing the defensive cover. Mourinho has even tried pairing Bernardo with Arda Guler in midfield , a move that helped the team turn the game around against PSV. Mourinho’s experiment with the 32-year-old midfielder seems to be paying off so far, and it remains to be seen how Bernardo fares over the course of the season.

Zaroury lobbed the ball over the Miami defense, Rodriguez controlled it, and a fraction of a second later it was off his foot for a goal that sent the Crew to the second round. Just like that, Rodriguez pumped his fists and booted the ball high into the Nordeke fan section. He also hit the "Gritty" dance celebration. Twice. Messi, meanwhile, stared in disbelief. Rodriguez, who goes by "Santi," was a fitting choice by fate to score the winner, and not just because it sent pulse rates soaring in Columbus. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram.
